requirements.name: go-stdlib-module
requirements.text: Implement in Go 1.22 or newer using only the standard library. The application root is a Go module, and its executable is the main package at `./cmd/csvstat`. Tests run under `go test`.

requirements.name: run-harness
requirements.text: `sources/run.sh` is the scoring entry point. It is supplied, not authored, and is staged verbatim into the application root with the data files. `drydock uat` runs `sh sources/run.sh` from the completed application root and takes its exit code and output as the score.

requirements.name: command-options
requirements.text:
csvstat [--column <name>] <file>
csvstat --freq <name> [--top <n>] <file>

requirements.name: column-option
requirements.text: `--column <name>` | Profile only the named column.

requirements.name: freq-top-options
requirements.text: `--freq <name>` | List the most frequent values of the named column instead of profiling.

requirements.name: option-combinations
requirements.text: `--column` and `--freq` cannot be combined. `--top` is valid only with `--freq`.

requirements.name: read-csv
requirements.text: The file is UTF-8 CSV as RFC 4180 defines it, read with Go's `encoding/csv`. The first record is the header.

requirements.name: trim-values
requirements.text: Every header name and every value is trimmed of leading and trailing spaces before any other rule applies.

requirements.name: reject-malformed-file
requirements.text: The file is **rejected** when it is empty, when a header name is empty or repeated, or when any record has a different number of fields from the header.

requirements.name: null-values
requirements.text: **Null.** A value is null when it is empty, or when it equals `NA`, `N/A`, or `NULL` ignoring case. All other values are non-null.

requirements.name: type-inference
requirements.text: A column's type is the first of these that every non-null value satisfies:

requirements.name: empty-type
requirements.text: A column with no non-null values has type `empty`.

requirements.name: profile-output
requirements.text: Header `column,type,rows,nulls,distinct,min,max,sum,mean,median`, then one row per column in file order (or the one named by `--column`).

requirements.name: count-fields
requirements.text: `rows` | Number of data records. `nulls` | Number of null values. `distinct` | Number of different non-null values, compared as exact strings after trimming.

requirements.name: min-max-fields
requirements.text: `min`, `max` | `integer`: the smallest and largest value as an integer. `number`: as a decimal. `date`: earliest and latest. `boolean`: `false` if any value is false, else `true`; `true` if any value is true, else `false`. `text`: smallest and largest by byte value. `empty`: empty.

requirements.name: numeric-stat-fields
requirements.text: `sum` | `integer`: the integer total. `number`: the decimal total. Otherwise empty. `mean` | `integer` and `number`: total divided by non-null count. Otherwise empty. `median` | `integer` and `number`: the middle value of the sorted non-null values, or the mean of the two middle values when the count is even. Otherwise empty.

requirements.name: decimal-formatting
requirements.text: **Decimals.** Every `number` `min`, `max`, and `sum`, and every `mean` and `median`, is written with exactly two decimal places, rounded half away from zero from the exact value, with a leading `-` when negative and no thousands separator: `1012.50`, `-12.21`, `0.00`. Integer `min`, `max`, and `sum` are written as plain integers.

requirements.name: frequency-output
requirements.text: Header `value,count`, then one row per distinct non-null value of the column, ordered by count descending, then value ascending by byte value, at most `--top` rows. Null values are not listed. A column with no non-null values writes only the header.

requirements.name: output-format
requirements.text: CSV on standard output with `\n` line endings. A field that contains a comma, a double quote, or a newline is quoted as RFC 4180 specifies; Go's `encoding/csv` writer produces this format.

requirements.name: failure-diagnostics
requirements.text: A failing command writes nothing to standard output and one diagnostic line to standard error naming the file and, for a rejected record, its line number.

requirements.name: exit-unreadable
requirements.text: `1` | Operational failure: the file cannot be opened or read.

requirements.name: exit-usage
requirements.text: `2` | Usage error: missing or extra file, unknown option, missing option value, `--top` not a positive integer, `--top` without `--freq`, `--column` with `--freq`.

requirements.name: exit-rejected
requirements.text: `3` | Rejected: empty file, empty or repeated header name, ragged record, or a column name that is not in the header.

requirements.name: test-script
requirements.text: The completed application provides a POSIX-compatible `bin/test.sh` that runs `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` from the application root and exits zero only when both pass. The suite covers each type, each statistic, null handling, rounding, each output form, and each exit code using files written by the tests.

requirements.name: profile-header-only-file
requirements.text: sku,price,in_stock

requirements.name: reject-ragged-records
requirements.text: A3,1.25,true,extra

requirements.name: build-csvstat-module
requirements.text: Builds ./cmd/csvstat with `go build`

requirements.name: profile-every-column
requirements.text: A. Every column of each data file

requirements.name: profile-one-column
requirements.text: B. One column

requirements.name: column-frequencies
requirements.text: C. Frequencies

requirements.text: check E1 3 "$DATA/ragged.csv" < /dev/null

requirements.name: unreadable-file-exit
requirements.text: check E4 1 "$MISSING" < /dev/null

requirements.name: usage-errors
requirements.text: U. Usage errors

requirements.name: conformance-gate
requirements.text: Exit 0 only when the build succeeds and every check passes.
